title: Nalwa Aero Flight-Tests Box-Wing Electric Aircraft in Punjab Milestone
excerpt: The Punjab startup's scaled eVTOL demonstrated hovering and forward flight with an all-tilting-rotor system, as it works towards a five-seat aircraft for passengers, air ambulances and cargo.
body:
• Punjab-based Nalwa Aero has flight-tested a scaled box-wing electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, demonstrating hovering and forward flight with electric propulsion and an all-tilting-rotor system.
  • Founder and CEO Kuljeet Singh Sandhu called it a world-first for an electric box-wing eVTOL with this configuration at this scale; the company has not disclosed the scaled aircraft's dimensions, flight count or trial duration.
  • The proposed full-size aircraft is a five-seat platform for passenger transport, air ambulances and cargo, with published targets of 350 km/h cruise, 450 km range and about 90 minutes endurance.
  • Nalwa Aero received DGCA Design Organisation Approval in June 2025 for eVTOL aircraft in the five-seat-and-above category, and its type certification application was accepted in January 2026 — certification itself is still ahead.

Indian startup Nalwa Aero has successfully flight-tested its scaled box-wing electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, demonstrating hovering and forward flight using electric propulsion and an all-tilting-rotor system. The tests mark the first successful flights of the company's unconventional design, which it hopes to develop into a five-seat platform for passenger transport, air ambulances and cargo operations, Aerospace Global News reported.

The company, based in Punjab, said the preliminary trials demonstrated that its wing arrangement could support both vertical and forward flight, an early step towards developing a full-sized aircraft. Founder and chief executive Kuljeet Singh Sandhu announced the flights on LinkedIn. "They said it was impossible. We believed otherwise. Today, we made it fly!" Sandhu wrote. "We believe this represents a WORLD-FIRST achievement – successfully demonstrating an electric Box-Wing eVTOL aircraft with this unique all-tilting-rotor configuration, not previously achieved anywhere in the world, to this scale."

How the box-wing design differs

Unlike most emerging electric air taxis, Nalwa Aero is pursuing a box-wing configuration in which the front and rear wings are connected at their tips, creating a closed structure around the aircraft. The design is intended to improve aerodynamic efficiency while providing structural strength for a relatively large electric aircraft. It draws on an aerodynamic concept explored more than a century ago by German scientist Ludwig Prandtl.

A conventional aircraft has a single main wing with a separate tailplane. Nalwa Aero's arrangement uses two lifting surfaces connected at their outer ends, intended to reduce losses from vortices at conventional wing tips and to distribute loads through the connected wings. For an electric aircraft, efficiency matters because battery weight limits range.

Nalwa Aero says preliminary internal studies suggest its design could deliver up to 40% greater aerodynamic efficiency than selected conventional configurations. That figure has not been independently validated through full-scale flight testing, and the company has described it as a potential improvement in certain aerodynamic parameters rather than a demonstrated increase in range, Aerospace Global News noted. Indian Startup Times reported the same preliminary figure and the same caution that it remains subject to experimental validation.

The proposed full-size aircraft

The proposed full-sized aircraft uses eight tilting rotors distributed across its front and rear wings, providing vertical thrust for take-off and landing before changing orientation to propel the aircraft forwards — lifting off like a helicopter, then flying forwards using its wings. The company has not specified whether the scaled trials included a complete transition between vertical and wing-borne flight.

Nalwa Aero is developing the larger aircraft under its Aphulas programme for passenger, medical, cargo and defence use. It lists maximum take-off weight of 4,000 kg and payload of 1,000 kg. Published targets include 350 km/h cruise, 450 km all-electric range and about 90 minutes endurance, with a hybrid hydrogen version envisaged beyond 1,500 km. It is also intended to incorporate fly-by-wire controls and autonomous capabilities.

Ministerial meeting and regulatory path

Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu welcomed the development after meeting Sandhu and chief technology officer Nelson Salas. "With such deep-tech innovations, we can transform urban mobility through flying taxis, air ambulances and even cargo flights, opening up exciting new possibilities!" the minister said. Indian Startup Times reported the same meeting and encouragement.

Sandhu recalled leaving Canada to pursue the project in India, and said Salas, who has more than 28 years of aircraft development experience, relocated from the United States to India with his family to join the programme. Nalwa Aero says it received Design Organisation Approval from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation in June 2025 for eVTOL aircraft in the five-seat-and-above category, and its application for type certification was accepted in January 2026.

Those steps do not mean the passenger aircraft is certified to enter service. Before commercial operations, Nalwa Aero must demonstrate its full-sized design's safety through further testing of propulsion, flight controls, batteries and structure. It has not announced a date for the full-scale aircraft's first flight or for certification.
